notes:
Reviews and Issues are redrawn, with a merge bar that concludes a request in one place. Discard a whole folder's changes, and on Windows and Linux Nori now runs on the same Git engine as the Mac app.

### Added

- Right-click a folder in the working copy and choose *Discard changes* to discard every change beneath it in that list, after a confirmation and with Undo.
- In a linked worktree's details, click a file to open its diff against the worktree's base, with committed, staged and new work included.
- With Pro, right-click a published branch in the sidebar or the graph and choose *Show pull request in Reviews* to open its pull or merge request.
- In a commit's details, a Reviews button beside each branch opens its pull or merge request; without Pro it is greyed beside the PRO badge.
- In Reviews, approve or unapprove a request and add it to the merge queue from the merge bar, enable auto-merge from its menu, and write comments with a Preview.
- Administrators of a GitHub repository can *Merge immediately* past what blocks a request, after a confirmation, never on a draft or a conflict.

### Changed

- Reviews and Issues are redrawn: two-line lists, a request header that leads with its state, a merge bar showing what blocks a merge, and titled fields in forms.
- On Windows and Linux, Nori runs on the Mac app's own Git engine, so repositories, Reviews and Issues behave the same on every platform.
- Closing a very large diff frees its memory at once, instead of keeping up to 600 MB for three minutes.
- Nori needs Git 2.30 or later instead of 2.36, and works in full with the Git that Ubuntu 22.04 and Debian 11 ship.

### Fixed

- A repository whose own Git settings name an SSH command, such as one picking a second SSH key, fetches automatically again instead of failing at every interval.
- A commit's or a stash's details open at once during a pull, a fetch or a commit, instead of waiting for it to finish.
- An approved request no longer reads "No review requested", and a bot's approval no longer shows an empty card.
- On Linux, from the AppImage, Git commands, links and files open without the AppImage's own libraries: branches list and clones work again.
- A long list of conflicted files scrolls instead of running past the window.
- On Windows and Linux, opening the closed requests in Reviews no longer leaves a blank window.
- With a Git older than 2.36, linked worktrees are listed again; with Git 2.30, reading a repository no longer fails.
- On Windows, settings, Undo history and your License are saved even while an antivirus is scanning the file.
- On Windows, opening a file in your editor no longer holds up a Git command started at the same moment until the editor closes.
